experiment.try: revisit the Ollama + Qwen tool-use bug (requirements.md step 5): diff the live qwen2.5-fixed model's chat template against C:\Code\test\pi-mono\qwen.fix, then test a real tool call
experiment.measure: does the TEMPLATE block match the reference patch; does a real POST /api/chat (Ollama's own API, port 11434) with a tools array actually produce a structured tool_calls reply
experiment.result: TEMPLATE block is byte-identical to qwen.fix (confirmed by diff; the only differences were ollama show's own auto-generated header/footer — the resolved FROM blob path, an inherited SYSTEM line, and the base model's LICENSE text, none of which is the template itself). So the earlier premise ("does the patch even match what's installed") is true: it does.

experiment.try: a real tool-enabled POST to qwen2.5-fixed (get_weather tool, "what's the weather in Boston")
experiment.result: 500 Internal Server Error, EMPTY body — no error message at all. Tried: fresh after `ollama stop` + reload (same 500), after `ollama create qwen2.5-fixed -f qwen.fix` from scratch (same 500), and — most telling — a PLAIN chat with no tools at all ALSO 500s on this model. So this is not a tool-schema problem: the patched chat template breaks Ollama's response handling for every request, tool-enabled or not. `ollama run qwen2.5-fixed "..."` (the CLI, not the HTTP API) returned nothing and no visible error either — same failure, no better diagnostics.

experiment.try: the SAME tool-enabled request against the UNPATCHED base model, qwen2.5-coder, as a control
experiment.result: 200 OK — but reproduces the ORIGINAL bug the patch was meant to fix: the model's reply has `message.content = '{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Boston"}}'` — a tool call, but as PLAIN TEXT content, not Ollama's structured `message.tool_calls` field (so a caller reading `tool_calls` the normal way sees nothing and the raw JSON just shows up as the model's words).

log.msg: Verdict for the open question ("since before this task"): the qwen.fix patch is correctly installed but does NOT fix the bug — it trades one failure for a worse one. Unpatched: tool call works but lands as unstructured text (the original bug). Patched: Ollama 500s on every request, tool or not, so nothing works at all. Neither qwen2.5-coder nor qwen2.5-fixed is usable for real tool calls through Ollama today. Not investigated further (time-boxed, lower priority than steps 1-4): WHY the patched template 500s — likely a Go template syntax Ollama's own engine chokes on (the `{{ end }}</tool_call>{{ end }}` closing sequence is a plausible suspect, untested) — Ollama gave no error text to confirm either way, and Ollama's own server log location wasn't located in this pass. Smallest next step: run Ollama in foreground (not as a background service) so its stderr is visible, send the same plain-chat request, and read the actual panic/error instead of guessing.

STOPPING here, per the brief, rather than chasing it further: two real gaps remain before this could actually work: (1) models/checkpoints/ in that install is EMPTY (only the placeholder put_checkpoints_here file) — no SD1.5, DreamShaper or any other checkpoint is present to generate anything with, and `requirements.md`'s own "what not to do" rules out downloading/touching checkpoints myself; (2) the Python environment main.py needs wasn't located — the install ships its own `uv` (resources/uv/win), suggesting the desktop app manages a private venv rather than using a system Python, but I did not find where. Smallest next step for whoever picks this up: find the venv uv created (a likely place: a sibling or child dir of the Electron app's own userData folder, not searched here), confirm an SD1.5 or DreamShaper checkpoint file exists somewhere on this machine (or get one), then try `<that venv>/python main.py --listen 127.0.0.1 --port <port>` by hand once, outside Servex, before building generate_image() around it.
